findings.description: The auto-backup callback is correctly wrapped in try/except, but it swallows EVERY exception type (bare `except Exception`) and only logs. For the current recorder that is fine, but a future on_backup that does real work (e.g. network/IO) will have failures silently absorbed with no signal to the caller. Also, `import logging` is performed inside the except handler on every failure; hoist it to module scope to match the rest of the codebase and avoid re-importing under error conditions.

`record()` mutates `app.config["last_auto_backup"]` from the watchdog observer/dispatch thread while Flask request threads read the same key in `_render_page` (gui.py:74) and `api_backup_last_auto` (routes_api.py:264). A single dict __setitem__ of a float is atomic under CPython's GIL so there is no tearing, but this cross-thread shared-state mutation is undocumented and fragile — a comment or an explicit lock/threading.Event would make the contract clear and survive an implementation change.

The PR claims a 'shared recorder', but `api_watcher_toggle` (line 159) and `api_watcher_save` (line 190) each construct a fresh `make_auto_backup_recorder(current_app._get_current_object())` per request rather than reusing the one created in `create_app` (gui.py:267). It is functionally harmless because all recorders close over the same app and write the same config key, but it contradicts the stated design and is wasted allocation. Consider stashing the recorder in app.config once and reusing it. The proxy-unwrapping via `_get_current_object()` is correct, though — that is the real fix and it is done right.

Seeding `_lastAuto = {{ last_auto_backup }}` correctly breaks the reload loop (server value == first poll value, so no immediate reload). However the unconditional `location.reload()` on any new auto-backup is a UX regression now that it actually fires: if the watcher backs up while the user has the settings overlay open or is mid-edit on a backup note, the full reload discards their in-progress input. Consider a non-destructive refresh of the backup list, or suppressing reload while a modal/input is active.

`api_backup_last_auto` returns a bare dict while every other endpoint in this module returns `jsonify(...)`. Flask serializes the dict correctly, so this is cosmetic, but the inconsistency is worth normalizing. The circular-import resolution (moving `register_api_routes` import into create_app at gui.py:270 so routes_api can import `make_auto_backup_recorder` at module top) is sound: gui.py no longer imports routes_api at module scope, so importing either module first is safe.

The regression test asserts `app.config["last_auto_backup"] > 0.0` after invoking the recorder outside a request context — this correctly pins the original bug (recorder must not depend on current_app/request). It is slightly weak: it never asserts the value equals a fresh time.time() reading or that the pre-call value was the 0.0 sentinel as the source of truth. Minor; the `assert not has_request_context()` guard is the valuable part.

summary: The core fix is correct and the verification is reproducible (confirmed 76 passed locally). The reload-loop bug is genuinely fixed by seeding `_lastAuto` from the server-rendered timestamp, the recorder is made request-context-independent and the API call sites correctly unwrap the app via `_get_current_object()`, the watcher callback failure is now logged instead of crashing the dispatch thread, and the circular import is properly broken by deferring the routes_api import into create_app. No correctness, security, or race-condition defects found. Remaining items are low-severity polish: cross-thread app.config mutation is undocumented (atomic under GIL, so not a bug), redundant per-request recorder construction contradicts the 'shared recorder' framing, and the unconditional location.reload() can clobber in-progress user input when an auto-backup lands.
